security_spec.violation_condition: In OpenSBI's HSM non-retentive suspend/resume flow (lib/sbi/sbi_hsm.c), the per-hart struct sbi_hsm_data saves MIE, MIP, MEDELEG, MIDELEG, and MENVCFG but does NOT save or restore mstateen0-3. Per the spec (norm:mstateen_zero_initialization), hardware resets all writable mstateen bits to zero on reset. After a deep suspend where the hart loses CSR state, mstateen0-3 come back as all-zero, losing bit 63 (STATEN) which controls access to sstateen/hstateen CSRs, and all other extension-enable bits (CONTEXT, IMSIC, AIA, ENVCFG, etc.) that OpenSBI originally set in mstatus_init(). Resume does not re-call mstatus_init(), so mstateen remains zeroed.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: HSM suspend/resume save/restore lists in sbi_hsm_data struct (and corresponding __sbi_hsm_hart_suspend/__sbi_hsm_hart_resume helpers) that include M-mode CSRs like menvcfg but omit mstateen0-3 CSR save/restore fields, or any resume path that fails to reinitialize mstateen after a non-retentive suspend where CSR state was lost
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI's HSM resume path fails to restore mstateen0-3 after non-retentive suspend, causing S-mode to lose access to all state controlled by these CSRs (sstateen, hstateen, IMSIC, AIA, context/environment config CSRs), violating the expectation that M-mode firmware transparently preserves hart state across suspend/resume cycles.

findings.finding: The struct omits mstateen0-3 save fields, but this is by design. mstateen0-3 do NOT need save/restore across non-retentive suspend because they are reinitialized from scratch by mstatus_init() in the warm-resume path (sbi_hart_reinit() → mstatus_init()), identically to how mstatus, mcounteren, scounteren, sstateen*, and hstateen* are handled. Only CSRs containing volatile S-mode-visible state (mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, menvcfg) need save/restore.

Correctly saves only the CSRs whose values may have been modified by S-mode (MIE, MIP.SSIP/STIP, MEDELEG, MIDELEG, MENVCFG). mstateen0-3 are not saved here because they are reinitialized from scratch by mstatus_init() during warm-resume — they contain static hardware-discovery-based values that don't change across suspend.

The warm-resume path calls sbi_hart_reinit() at line 490 before CSR restore at line 498. sbi_hart_reinit() calls mstatus_init(), which reinitializes mstateen0-3, sstateen*, hstateen*, menvcfg, mstatus, and other CSRs. The subsequent __sbi_hsm_suspend_non_ret_restore() then overlays saved mie/mip/medeleg/mideleg/menvcfg. mstateen0-3 are correctly set before the hart switches back to S-mode via mret. No window of vulnerability exists.

Calls mstatus_init() unconditionally, which fully reinitializes mstateen0-3 with STATEN, CONTEXT, HSENVCFG, and optionally AIA/IMSIC/SVSLCT/CTR/SRMCFG based on extension detection. This is the mechanism that ensures mstateen is correctly configured after hardware reset clears all bits. No separate save/restore is needed because the values are deterministically recomputed.

Reinitializes mstateen0 with extension-specific enable bits and mstateen1-3 with STATEN only. Also zeroes sstateen0-3 and hstateen0-3 (lines 122-135). These writes execute during warm-resume before S-mode is re-entered, so the hardware-reset-induced all-zero state is correctly repaired. Compliant with norm:mstateen_zero_initialization expectations.

Called after sbi_hart_reinit() (which reinitializes mstateen). Only restores volatile CSR values (menvcfg, mideleg, medeleg, mie, mip) that S-mode may have changed. mstateen0-3 were already correctly configured by the preceding mstatus_init() call and are not overwritten. The ordering is correct: reinit static CSRs first, then overlay saved volatile state, then mret to S-mode.
